      42:05Those two clusters came without looking at the two black dots.

      42:19So that's a natural place to say, OK, what if I did this

      42:25That's what I get.

      43:26Having done three, I could say should I look for four?
      43:28Well, those points down there, as I've already said,

      43:34And I don't want to overfit.

      43:43Let me finish with showing you one other example
      43:46from the other direction.
      43:47Which is, suppose I give you labeled examples.
      43:52So again, the goal is I've got features
      43:54associated with each example.

      43:57But I also know the label associated with them.
      43:59And I want to learn what is the best
      44:01way to come up with a rule that will let me take new examples
      44:04and assign them to the right group.
      44:07A number of ways to do this.
      44:08You can simply say I'm looking for the simplest surface that

      44:13In my football case that were in the plane, what's

      44:19I might look for a more complicated surface.

      44:27Because there's not just one line that does the separation.

      44:38And you're going to see next time.
      44:39I'm going to just highlight it here.
      44:40There's a third way, which will lead

      44:43called k nearest neighbors.
      44:46And the idea here is I've got a set of labeled data.

      47:13And here is the actual label.

      48:02I labeled it as not being an instance, and it is.
